areas.name: Table Mountain
areas.advice: Two stabbings on the lower Deer Park–Tafelberg Road slopes within a week (8 and ~13 Jul) — avoid the quieter lower-slope paths alone, especially early morning; patrols have been increased.

areas.name: Lion's Head
areas.advice: Busy and sociable in daylight; for sunrise or sunset go up with company and head down before dark.

areas.name: Signal Hill
areas.advice: Crime was reported here in recent weeks — go in a group and stick to the busier summit paths; the Lion's Head Jeep Track's autumn maintenance closure had not been confirmed lifted as of 9 Jul.

areas.name: Newlands Forest
areas.advice: A knife-threat was reported in the forest in late June — walk the lower forest in groups and leave nothing visible in your car.

trailheads.name: Lion's Head parking, Signal Hill Rd

parking.note: Roadside bays with a smash-and-grab history — take everything with you, leave the car visibly empty.
Busier and marshalled in cableway hours; still leave nothing visible.
Fine when busy; gets quiet outside peak hours.
High turnover on clear days; quiet mid-week mornings — nothing visible in the car.
Sunset crowds attract pickpockets and car-window opportunists.
History of remote-jamming theft and vehicle theft — double-check your doors actually locked, take valuables with you.
Quiet lot on the Vredehoek fringe — park on busy days only, or start elsewhere.

incidents.location_text: Near the Platteklip Wash Houses, Deer Park area
incidents.summary: Man mugged and stabbed near the Platteklip Wash Houses — the second stabbing on the lower slopes within a week; patrols increased.

incidents.location_text: Deadman's Tree area, near Tafelberg Road
incidents.summary: Runner stabbed in the forearm by three armed men near Deadman's Tree; he fought them off and nothing was taken. SAPS case opened.

incidents.location_text: Lion's Head parking area, Signal Hill Rd
incidents.summary: Suspect caught fleeing after stealing from a parked vehicle at the Lion's Head parking area; stolen items recovered.
Hiker threatened with a knife in Newlands Forest; the victim was reportedly turned away when trying to report it at SAPS Claremont.
Unspecified crimes reported around Signal Hill over recent weeks.

incidents.location_text: The Glen Trail, between Kloof Nek and Camps Bay
incidents.summary: Couple assaulted and robbed by armed men on The Glen trail; one hiker stabbed. Reported to rangers; SANParks issued an alert.

routes.name: Platteklip Gorge
routes.description: The classic direct ascent — a relentless stone-stepped climb up the gorge to the plateau; descend by cableway.
routes.source_name: Hike Table Mountain (Tim Lundy) — Platteklip Gorge route page
advice: Carry at least two litres of water for the climb.
No scrambling or exposure on this route, but the climb is sustained — pace yourself.
Cableway descent isn't guaranteed — check it's running before you rely on it.

routes.name: Platteklip Gorge to Maclear's Beacon
routes.description: Platteklip's climb, then left across the plateau to the summit beacon at 1086 m.
routes.source_name: Forge (forgesa.com) — Maclears Beacon via Platteklip Gorge route page
advice: Carry enough water for the ascent — the gorge climb can get very warm.
Underfoot is a long series of rocky zig-zags in the gorge section.

routes.name: India Venster

end.name: Plateau top-out at the head of Platteklip Gorge

routes.description: The adventurous line under the cableway — chains, staples and real exposure; ascend only, never descend it.
routes.source_name: Hike Table Mountain (Tim Lundy) — India Venster route page
advice: Descending India Venster isn't advised — go down by cableway or via Platteklip instead.
Narrow ledges add to the exposure; this route needs a decent head for heights.
A guide is worth considering if you're a less confident scrambler; not suited to significant fear of heights.

routes.name: Kasteelspoort
routes.description: Twelve Apostles ravine from Theresa Ave via the Pipe Track — rock steps and light scrambling to the Back Table.
routes.source_name: Hike Table Mountain (Tim Lundy) — Kasteelspoort route page
advice: Steel ladders near Echo Valley add some exposure on the standard line; a no-exposure alternative exists.
The path dries off quickly after rain, unlike some of the mountain's other ravines.

routes.name: Pipe Track
routes.description: A gentle contour walk along the Twelve Apostles flank — little climbing, limited shade.
routes.source_name: Hike Addicts — The Pipe Track Hiking Route on Table Mountain
advice: Starts at the grass patch where Kloof Nek Road meets Tafelberg Road.
Rock path transitioning to jeep track with stone steps — easy going, but it covers real distance, so come prepared.

routes.name: Skeleton Gorge to Maclear's Beacon

start.name: Contour Path above Kirstenbosch (Skeleton Gorge gate)

routes.description: Ladders and stream boulders up Skeleton Gorge, then Smuts Track to the beacon; access through Kirstenbosch.
routes.source_name: SANBI Kirstenbosch — Smuts Track up Skeleton Gorge (safety-on-the-mountain page)
advice: Garden gates open at 8am, so your start time is gated by Kirstenbosch's opening hours.

access.name: Kirstenbosch Gate 2
access.note: Enter Kirstenbosch Garden at Gate 2 — garden entry fee and hours apply (gates open 8am). The path starts at the top of the garden.

routes.name: Skeleton Gorge / Nursery Ravine loop

start.name: Contour Path above Kirstenbosch (Skeleton Gorge gate)

end.name: Contour Path above Kirstenbosch (Skeleton Gorge gate)

routes.description: Up Skeleton, across the Back Table past the dam, down Nursery Ravine — SANBI's two 'safe routes' paired.
routes.source_name: SANBI Kirstenbosch — Smuts Track up Skeleton Gorge (safety-on-the-mountain page)
advice: Nursery Ravine, the descent, is steep and strenuous with mostly stepped path underfoot.
Starts inside Kirstenbosch at Gate 2 — entry fee and garden hours apply.

access.name: Kirstenbosch Gate 2
access.note: Enter Kirstenbosch Garden at Gate 2 — garden entry fee and hours apply (gates open 8am). The path starts at the top of the garden.

routes.name: Lion's Head Summit Path

start.name: Lion's Head parking, Signal Hill Rd

routes.description: The famous spiral to the summit — ladders, staples and chains near the top; same path down.
routes.source_name: Hike Table Mountain (Tim Lundy) — Lion's Head
advice: A slightly longer alternative path avoids the most exposed climbing near the top, if you'd rather skip the chains.
The descent can be more challenging than the ascent — it demands balance and a head for heights.
Carry at least a litre of water — there's no water source on the mountain.

routes.name: Signal Hill summit walk

start.name: Lion's Head parking, Signal Hill Rd (Kloof Nek side)

routes.description: An easy ridge stroll from the Lion's Head parking side to the summit viewpoint — no real hiking required.
advice: A well-known, low-effort sunset spot — quieter than Lion's Head.
Paths criss-cross the hilltop through indigenous vegetation, rather than a single defined trail.

routes.name: Woodcutters Trail loop
routes.description: A shaded Newlands Forest circuit — steady climb to Woodcutters Trail, looping back down through the forest.
routes.source_name: Hiking in the South — Woodcutters Trail
advice: Paths are well-established and easy to follow throughout the loop.

routes.name: Newlands Ravine
routes.description: Steep shaded switchbacks from Newlands Forest to the Saddle — the easiest eastside way up.
routes.source_name: Extra Time Media — Newlands Forest hikes: Newlands Ravine route
advice: Starts on the Contour Path opposite the wooden picnic spot above Newlands Forest Station.
Check a map before descending and keep GPS handy — several routes join at the Saddle.
Steep, slippery and rocky underfoot on the way down — not a first trail outing.

routes.name: Kloof Corner lookout
routes.description: Short steep steps to the ridge lookout — a 30-minute sunset classic; stops before the chained scramble.
routes.source_name: The Hiking Chronicles — Kloof Corner Hike from Tafelberg Road
advice: The small Tafelberg Road parking area fills quickly around sunset in summer.
Bring a torch or headlamp if you'll be descending after sunset; bring water even though the route is short.
Can be windy at the lookout, even when it's calm below.

routes.name: Summit Stroll
routes.description: Cableway up, then a near-level loop across the Table to Maclear's Beacon and back along the quieter plateau path — the summit without the climb; cableway down.
routes.source_name: Hike Table Mountain (Tim Lundy) — Summit Stroll route page
advice: Cableway both ways — if cloud or wind close it while you're up, the walk down is Platteklip Gorge: a steep stepped descent of around two hours.
One short stretch along the front rim has mild exposure; the inland path avoids it.
Heavy cloud or strong wind cancels this walk — the guide that runs it won't go up in either.

access.name: Lower Cable Station, Tafelberg Rd
access.note: Take the cable car up — the walk starts at the top station.

routes.name: Corridor Ravine / Kasteelspoort loop
routes.description: The Twelve Apostles circuit — Pipe Track south to Corridor Ravine, up onto the Back Table, along the Apostles path and down Kasteelspoort to Theresa Avenue.
routes.source_name: Ridgway Ramblers — Hike along the 12 Apostles on Table Mountain
advice: About four hours for the circuit — the climb up Corridor Ravine and the descent of Kasteelspoort are the work; the Back Table between them is relatively flat.
Steel ladders near Echo Valley add some exposure on the standard Kasteelspoort line; a no-exposure alternative exists.
Four hours with a long climb — carry at least two litres.

route_conditions.line: Exposed with full sun most of the day and little shelter — heat builds fast on this climb.
Chains and exposed rock — postpone in strong wind; wind can also stop the cableway you'd descend by.
Wet rock here is dangerous — postpone if rain is forecast or has recently fallen.
No shade and nowhere to refill on the ravine climb — heat builds fast.
Limited shade along the Twelve Apostles flank — go early morning or evening in hot weather.
Very slippery in winter and after heavy rain — can be practically impassable straight after a heavy downpour.
Seasonal streams make the Skeleton Gorge section slippery in winter and after rain.
Ladders, staples and chains near the top turn risky in strong wind — consider postponing.
Chains and rock near the summit get slick in the rain — a guiding source flags rain as the most dangerous condition here.
Strong wind stops the cableway — check it's running before you go up, and know that Platteklip Gorge is the walk down.
Heavy cloud or rain: the guide cancels this walk in either — the cableway may close and the plateau loses its views.
A four-hour circuit with a long climb — heat builds on Corridor Ravine's open steps; start early and carry extra water.
